instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Use MathWorld Fibonacci Number page as source
criteria.description: Agent uses the MathWorld page (https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FibonacciNumber.html) as the source of truth for all reported items. Full credit if the agent clearly bases the recurrence, initial conditions, first eight positive-index Fibonacci numbers, and OEIS identifier on the MathWorld page. Full credit also if the agent makes a reasonable attempt to access MathWorld but it is inaccessible (down/CAPTCHA/error/block) and the agent explicitly reports the blocker and that it cannot proceed within constraints. No credit if the agent reports values from memory or other sources without attempting/using MathWorld when it is accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the Wolfram MathWorld page titled “Fibonacci Number” with the definition text containing the recurrence, initial-condition statements, the initial terms list, and the OEIS reference. Screenshot 2 is farther down the same page (pop-culture section) and is not needed for the requested extraction. Latest relevant evidence: Screenshot 2 still confirms it is the same MathWorld page, but Screenshot 1 contains the target data.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent’s output explicitly attributes the recurrence/initial conditions/terms/OEIS ID to the MathWorld Fibonacci Number page, and Screenshot 1 confirms those items are present on that page. No blocker is shown. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot clearly shows the Wolfram MathWorld site header (“Wolfram MathWorld”), and the page title “Fibonacci Number.” The visible body text discusses “The Fibonacci numbers are the sequence of numbers {F_n}… defined by the linear recurrence equation” and shows the recurrence formula and the sequence sentence including an OEIS reference.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms the agent is using the MathWorld “Fibonacci Number” page content as the source: the recurrence, initial conditions statement, and OEIS link text are visibly present on this MathWorld page. This supports full credit for sourcing.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the agent cites the MathWorld Fibonacci Number page, which matches what is visible in the screenshot (MathWorld branding and Fibonacci Number page content).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a mid-page section of MathWorld content discussing pop-culture references to Fibonacci numbers. Visible text includes: “The above cartoon (Amend 2005) shows an unconventional sports application of the Fibonacci numbers … (The right panel instead applies the Perrin sequence).” It also mentions a scrambled version “13, 3, 2, 21, 1, 1, 8, 5 (OEIS A117540)” in the context of The Da Vinci Code, and references TV episodes (“Sabotage” from NUMB3RS and “Masterpiece” from Criminal Minds) and a “golden spiral.” Below, there is a large triangular black-and-white plotted graphic. A caption begins: “The plot above shows the first 511 terms of the Fibonacci sequence represented in binary…” A cookie consent bar at the bottom reads: “This website uses cookies…” with an “Accept & Close” button. The screenshot does NOT show the Fibonacci recurrence formula, initial conditions, the list of the first eight Fibonacci numbers, or an OEIS identifier for the main Fibonacci sequence on the page.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion 0 requires that the reported recurrence, initial conditions, first eight positive-index terms (F1–F8), and the OEIS identifier come from the MathWorld Fibonacci Number page. This screenshot provides no visible evidence of the recurrence or initial conditions or the F1–F8 list. It does show an OEIS identifier (A117540) but that is explicitly for a scrambled version of the first eight Fibonacci numbers, not the main Fibonacci sequence’s OEIS entry. Therefore, the screenshot cannot substantiate the agent’s predicted output items (recurrence, initial conditions, F1–F8 list, and OEIS A000045) as being taken from the MathWorld page content visible here.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims the page displays: recurrence “F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2),” initial conditions including “F_0 = 0” and “F_1 = F_2 = 1,” first eight positive-index terms through 21, and OEIS “A000045.” None of those elements are visible in this screenshot. The only OEIS identifier visible in the screenshot is “OEIS A117540,” which contradicts the agent’s assertion that the visible OEIS reference is A000045 (at least for this captured view).

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 shows URL https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FibonacciNumber.html with title “Fibonacci Number -- from Wolfram MathWorld,” confirming the MathWorld page is loaded and available as the source.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent explicitly cites the MathWorld Fibonacci Number page as the sole source and nothing in the DOM evidence contradicts that. No access blocker is shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL "https://mathworld.wolfram.com/FibonacciNumber.html" with Title "Fibonacci Number -- from Wolfram MathWorld" under the DOM snapshot header.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM model explicitly shows the agent is on the MathWorld "Fibonacci Number" page at the specified URL, so using this page as the source of truth is supported by the captured state.

criteria.description: Report the Fibonacci recurrence exactly as displayed on the MathWorld page, preserving mathematical notation. Full credit for the correct recurrence with exact symbols/formatting as shown. Partial credit if the correct relationship is given but notation deviates from MathWorld’s display. If MathWorld is inaccessible after a reasonable attempt and the agent clearly reports the access blocker, award full credit for this criterion (since extraction is impossible). No credit if the recurrence is incorrect/missing when MathWorld is accessible or if the agent fabricates content.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 displays the recurrence as an inline equation: “F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2}” with an equation number “(1)”.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported the recurrence as “F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2)”, which matches the mathematical content shown in Screenshot 1 (minor formatting differences in how subscripts are typed in plain text are acceptable). Award full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the main text, the displayed recurrence appears as “F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2)” (rendered as F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2}) with an equation label “(1)” to the right.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output states “F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2),” which matches the recurrence shown in the screenshot. Notation is consistent with what is visible (subscripts n-1 and n-2).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Minor wording discrepancy: the agent references “from Table 1,” but the screenshot shows it in the page text with equation number “(1)” (not a table). The recurrence itself matches what is shown.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 Table 1 displays the recurrence exactly as “F_n=F_(n-1)+F_(n-2)” (with equation label (1)).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported the correct recurrence but added spaces around operators (“F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2)”) rather than preserving the exact displayed string formatting. This is a minor notation/formatting deviation, so a small deduction is warranted rather than a major penalty.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0, TABLES -> Table 1 contains the recurrence: "F_n=F_(n-1)+F_(n-2) | (1)". Also VISIBLE CONTENT includes: "The Fibonacci numbers are the sequence of numbers defined by the linear recurrence equation" followed by the displayed table.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The recurrence is explicitly present in the DOM table as "F_n=F_(n-1)+F_(n-2)" (equation (1)), matching the agent’s reported recurrence form.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output included spaces and parentheses in subscripts ("F_n = F_(n-1) + F_(n-2)") whereas the table text is rendered without spaces ("F_n=F_(n-1)+F_(n-2)"). This is a minor formatting deviation from the exact DOM text.

criteria.description: Report the initial conditions exactly as displayed on the MathWorld page, preserving mathematical notation. Full credit for both initial conditions exactly as shown. Partial credit if initial conditions are correct but not in MathWorld’s displayed form. If MathWorld is inaccessible after a reasonable attempt and the agent clearly reports the access blocker, award full credit for this criterion. No credit if incorrect/missing when MathWorld is accessible or if the agent fabricates content.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 text immediately after the recurrence states: “with F_1 = F_2 = 1. As a result of the definition (1), it is conventional to define F_0 = 0.”
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported initial conditions “F_0 = 0” and “F_1 = F_2 = 1,” which matches Screenshot 1 exactly. The agent’s note about it coming from an image (vs prose) is a nitpick and does not affect correctness. Upgrade to full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Immediately below the recurrence, the text reads: “with F_1 = F_2 = 1. As a result of the definition (1), it is conventional to define F_0 = 0.”
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output lists initial conditions as “F_0 = 0” and “F_1 = F_2 = 1,” which are exactly the conditions visible in the screenshot (same symbols and equality).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent claims “from the labeled image on the page,” but the screenshot evidence for initial conditions is in the paragraph text, not an image. The values/notation themselves align with what is visible.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 media/image labels explicitly include both initial-condition strings: “F_0=0” and “F_1=F_2=1.”
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent’s initial conditions match what is explicitly displayed in the DOM evidence (including “F_1=F_2=1”). Baseline’s deduction was based on an incorrect assumption; adjust to full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0, MEDIA / IMAGE LABELS include initial-condition text strings: "F_1=F_2=1" and "F_0=0".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM provides explicit labels for the initial conditions via image/figure labels: "F_0=0" and "F_1=F_2=1". These support the agent’s recorded initial conditions.

criteria.criterion: Report first eight positive-index Fibonacci numbers (F1–F8 only)
criteria.description: List the first eight positive-index terms as F1 through F8 (exclude F0), matching the MathWorld page’s displayed sequence values. Full credit if all eight terms are correct and correspond to F1–F8. Partial credit if 5–7 terms are correct or if F0 is incorrectly included but the F1–F8 values are otherwise present. If MathWorld is inaccessible after a reasonable attempt and the agent clearly reports the access blocker, award full credit for this criterion. No credit if fewer than 5 correct terms when MathWorld is accessible or if the agent fabricates content.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 states: “The Fibonacci numbers for n = 1, 2, ... are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ... (OEIS A000045).” This provides F1–F8 directly.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent listed F1 through F8 as 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, correctly excluding F0 from the eight requested terms. Full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The page text states: “The Fibonacci numbers for n = 1, 2, ... are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ... (OEIS A000045).” These first eight numbers are visible in order.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output lists F1–F8 as 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, which matches the first eight positive-index terms shown in the screenshot sequence for n=1,2,…. The agent also correctly excludes F0 from the eight-term list while separately noting F0 in initial conditions.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No substantive discrepancy: the sequence values match what is visible, and the mapping to F1–F8 is consistent with the screenshot’s “for n=1,2,...” statement.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 visible content states: “The Fibonacci numbers for , 2, ... are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ...” which provides the first eight positive-index values in order.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent listed F1–F8 as 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, which matches the DOM-listed first eight values for positive indices. Even though the page presents them as an ordered list rather than explicit per-index equalities, the requested terms are correctly delivered.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0, VISIBLE CONTENT includes: "The Fibonacci numbers for , 2, ... are 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ... (OEIS A000045 )."
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM explicitly lists the first eight positive-index values as the sequence "1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21" for the Fibonacci numbers (for positive indices). This supports the numeric terms, but the DOM snippet does not explicitly map each value to the labeled equalities "F_1 = 1" through "F_8 = 21" in-text (it provides the ordered list rather than per-term assignments).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output presents an explicit mapping (F1=1 ... F8=21). The DOM evidence supports the ordered values but does not explicitly show the per-index equality formatting.

criteria.criterion: Report linked OEIS identifier (exact as displayed)
criteria.description: Provide the OEIS identifier linked from the MathWorld page for the Fibonacci sequence, preserving the identifier exactly as displayed (e.g., formatting like 'Axxxxxx'). Full credit for the exact identifier. Partial credit if the correct OEIS entry is referenced but the identifier is not preserved exactly (typo/formatting). If MathWorld is inaccessible after a reasonable attempt and the agent clearly reports the access blocker, award full credit for this criterion. No credit if missing/wrong when MathWorld is accessible or if the agent fabricates content.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the primary sequence sentence ending with “(OEIS A000045).” Screenshot 2 shows a different OEIS ID (A117540) but in a different context (scrambled sequence) and is not the one attached to the main Fibonacci definition.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported the linked OEIS identifier for the main Fibonacci sequence as “A000045,” matching Screenshot 1 exactly. Full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The sequence sentence ends with “(OEIS A000045).” The identifier “A000045” is visible as part of the OEIS reference.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent reports the OEIS identifier as “A000045,” matching exactly what is displayed in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None: the OEIS identifier matches the screenshot text exactly.

dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent reported the OEIS identifier exactly as displayed: “A000045.”

criteria.criterion: Respect stopping condition and scope constraints
criteria.description: Agent stops after recording: recurrence, initial conditions, first eight positive-index terms (F1–F8), and OEIS identifier; does not add unrelated information or follow unrelated external links. Full credit if the response contains only the requested items (and no extra exploration/output beyond them). Partial credit if minor extra irrelevant content is included but requested items are present (or, if blocked, the agent stops after reporting the blocker). No credit if the agent omits requested items due to excessive unrelated navigation/content, follows unrelated links, or fails to stop appropriately.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: No screenshot evidence suggests the agent followed unrelated links or included extraneous information. The agent’s predicted output contains only the recurrence, initial conditions, F1–F8 terms, and the OEIS identifier (plus minimal labeling/URL).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Meets the stopping condition and scope constraints: no unrelated external links followed, and output stays within requested items. Full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows additional content beyond the requested items (site navigation sidebar, links to Fibonacci polynomials/Lucas sequence, and a comic image area beginning below), indicating the page contains more than the recurrence/terms/OEIS reference. The agent’s predicted output text (provided above) includes only recurrence, initial conditions, F1–F8 values, and OEIS identifier (plus the page URL and brief labels).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent’s predicted output appears to respect scope: it provides exactly the requested mathematical items and the OEIS ID, without unrelated exploration or following external links. Including the URL and section labels is minor and does not violate the stopping condition.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No mismatch with the screenshot regarding scope. The only slight issue is the agent’s references to “Table 1” and “labeled image,” but they did not add unrelated content beyond the requested fields.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 0 shows the needed items are on-page; action history shows only a scroll action and no link-following. Agent output includes only the recurrence, initial conditions, first eight positive-index terms, and OEIS identifier (with minimal provenance text).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent stayed within scope and stopping condition: no unrelated navigation and no extraneous mathematical facts beyond the requested items.
